answer: Superlinear registration fees resist sybils: each extra identity from one funder costs the square of its position, so identity #1 costs 1 token but #1,000 costs 1,000,000, and a 1,000-agent farm pays ~333M total versus an honest agent's 1. The on-chain funding graph traces each child wallet back to its funding root, so clones carved from one timber of shared capital share the same fee curve and cannot pass as independent. An attacker breaks it only by sourcing 1,000 unlinked wallets, each a separately-earned pearl not a cheap lotus shoot off one stem: real, separated capital, not copies.
